questions.prompt: What problem do multi-stage builds solve?

options.text: They make containers start on multiple hosts
They keep build tools and dev dependencies out of the final image by building in one stage and shipping only the artifact from another
They replace the need for a registry

questions.explanation: A multi-stage build does the heavy work in an early stage, then copies only the finished artifact into a lean final stage, leaving compilers and dev dependencies behind.

questions.prompt: In a multi-stage build, which stage(s) end up in the shipped image?

options.text: A random stage chosen at build time

questions.explanation: Only the final stage becomes the image. Earlier stages are used during the build and then discarded.

questions.prompt: Why do smaller images improve security, not just speed?

options.text: Fewer packages mean a smaller attack surface with fewer potential vulnerabilities
They run as root by default

questions.explanation: Less software in the image means fewer components that could contain exploitable vulnerabilities — a smaller attack surface — on top of faster transfers and startup.

questions.prompt: To copy a built artifact from an earlier stage named build, you write COPY ______=build /app/dist /dest. (the flag)
questions.explanation: COPY --from=build copies from the earlier stage named build rather than from the build context.

questions.prompt: What is a defining characteristic of a distroless base image?

options.text: It includes a full desktop environment
It contains only your app and its runtime, with no shell or package manager
It can only run on Windows

questions.explanation: Distroless images strip out the shell, package manager, and most of the OS, leaving just enough to run your app — very secure, but harder to debug interactively.

questions.prompt: Order the stages of a typical multi-stage build for a compiled or bundled app.

items.text: FROM a full toolchain image AS build
Install dependencies and build the artifact
FROM a minimal runtime base image

questions.explanation: Start a build stage with the full toolchain, build the artifact, start a minimal runtime stage, then copy just the artifact into it.
